tldr_label: TL;DR — Post-midterm Iran strike plans, an AI sell-off and Brent above $113 rattle markets

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: ABC and the New York Times report the US and Israel have drawn up plans to resume strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms; the White House says there will be no attack before then. [[TAG:danger:strike plans]]

tldr_bullets.label: Hormuz
tldr_bullets.body: CENTCOM rejected Iran's claim that seven ships were hit, saying 95% of vessels get through; Trump said Iran is 'making up fake hits'. Trackers show traffic near zero.

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The Nasdaq fell 2.6%, its worst day since June, as Meta dropped about 7% and chip stocks sank; Brent topped $113. [[TAG:danger:Nasdaq -2.6%]]

tldr_bullets.label: Saudi Arabia
tldr_bullets.body: Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters for the first time in the war, a day after an attack on Dammam's airport killed two.

tldr_bullets.label: France
tldr_bullets.body: French 10-year yields rose above 5% and above US Treasuries for the first time since 2013 amid budget and protest turmoil.

tldr_bullets.label: Elections
tldr_bullets.body: Israel votes Tuesday with polls deadlocked; Brazil's Sunday runoff between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula is a statistical tie.

sections.title: Iran War and the Strait of Hormuz
sections.summary: US and Israel reportedly plan post-midterm strikes; CENTCOM disputes Iran's seven-ship claim

paragraphs.heading: Strike plans
paragraphs.body: Two Israeli sources told ABC News that the US and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for joint strikes on Iran, almost certainly after the November 3 midterms, with targets including petrochemical facilities and the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site; the New York Times first reported the planning. Some officials told the Times that Trump would steer strikes away from oil infrastructure. The White House said the US 'will not be attacking Iran' before the election. [[TAG:danger:post-midterm strikes]]

paragraphs.heading: Disputed attacks
paragraphs.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said seven tankers were hit, which would be the largest single-day toll of the war, Al Jazeera reported. A CENTCOM spokesperson called the mine claims incorrect and said 95% of vessels get through, and Trump said Iran is 'making up fake hits' to raise oil prices before the midterms, the Times of Israel reported. Independent trackers such as straits.live show commercial traffic at a small fraction of prewar levels. [[TAG:warning:conflicting claims]]

paragraphs.heading: Offensive doctrine
paragraphs.body: The IRGC said renewed US attacks could prompt Iran to invade neighboring countries and hit bases used in US operations, Al Jazeera reported, as it threatened US bases if Washington keeps escorting ships through Hormuz. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still wants a deal but is ready for war.

sections.sources: ABC News, Times of Israel, Al Jazeera, Fox News, NBC News, straits.live

sections.title: Saudi Arabia Under Fire
sections.summary: Aramco clears its Dhahran HQ; Houthi attack on Dammam airport kills two; Saudi stocks slide

paragraphs.heading: Aramco evacuation
paragraphs.body: Saudi Aramco ordered staff out of its Dhahran headquarters to work remotely, the first such order since the Iran war began, Reuters reported citing six sources, via TimesLIVE and Gulf News. Reports differ on the trigger; one said an alarm prompted it. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index fell 2.5% on the news, according to LSEG data. [[TAG:warning:HQ evacuated]]

paragraphs.heading: Dammam airport
paragraphs.body: A Houthi attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed two people, a Saudi and an Indian national, and wounded eight, before operations resumed, Al Jazeera reported. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed four drones over Riyadh and Medina, and Saudi Arabia has struck Houthi missile launcher sites, The Jerusalem Post reported. [[TAG:danger:2 killed]]

sections.title: Markets: AI Sell-off Meets Oil Spike
sections.summary: Nasdaq posts worst day since June as Meta and chips sink; Brent tops $113; Asia extends losses

paragraphs.heading: Thursday's close
paragraphs.body: The Nasdaq fell about 2.6% to roughly 26,009, its worst session since June, and the S&P 500 lost 1.21% to 7,663.43, while the Dow edged up 0.02% to 52,867.98, CNBC and Yahoo Finance reported. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell about 7%, Investrade reported, and chip and AI stocks made up 93% of the Nasdaq-100's lost value, according to Stocktitan. [[TAG:danger:SOX about -7%]]

paragraphs.heading: Meta
paragraphs.body: Meta shares fell about 7% as investors focused on $34.9 billion of quarterly capex and negative free cash flow rather than its revenue beat, Yahoo Finance reported. NBC News said reports of post-midterm Iran strike plans added to the sell-off.

paragraphs.heading: Oil and gold
paragraphs.body: Brent reached $113.21 by 8 a.m. Eastern on Thursday, about $2.47 above the prior morning, Fortune reported; Oilprice.com showed it near $114. In Asia on Friday, the Kospi fell about 2.2%, the Kosdaq 3.5% and China's CSI300 hit its lowest since July 2025, investingLive reported, while gold slipped below $4,000 an ounce for the first time since July. [[TAG:warning:Brent ~$113]]

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Russia fires 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv hours after agreeing to resume talks

paragraphs.heading: Kyiv barrage
paragraphs.body: Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv in three waves, hours after Putin agreed in principle to resume trilateral talks, Zelenskyy said, according to ABC News and NBC News. Ukraine's air force said none of the missiles were intercepted. Tolls vary: the AP reported at least four killed across Ukraine, including two in a strike on a Kharkiv-region market, while Kyiv's toll was put at one or two dead. [[TAG:danger:none intercepted]]

paragraphs.heading: Drones on Moscow
paragraphs.body: Moscow said it downed more than 800 Ukrainian drones, including about 630 aimed at the capital, PBS and The Globe and Mail reported. Witkoff said trilateral talks would continue at a technical level, The Japan Times reported.

sections.sources: ABC News, NBC News, AP via PBS, The Globe and Mail, The Japan Times

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Trump rallies in Iowa for Senate hopeful Ashley Hinson; judge orders BBC suit deposition

paragraphs.heading: Iowa rally
paragraphs.body: Trump rallied in Sioux City with Senate nominee Ashley Hinson and gubernatorial nominee Zach Lahn, Fox News and CBS Iowa reported. NBC News rates Hinson's race against Democrat Josh Turek a toss-up. Trump touted emergency diesel tax relief and a new $8 billion agricultural aid program, Fox News reported. [[TAG:info:toss-up race]]

paragraphs.heading: Other threads
paragraphs.body: A judge ordered Trump to sit for a deposition by December 11 in his defamation suit against the BBC, and administration lawyers said construction of a large arch could begin as soon as November 5, according to the Washington Post's Trump coverage. CNN reported Trump defended an Ohio ad by Vivek Ramaswamy featuring rival Amy Acton's estranged mother.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: French 10-year yield tops 5% and US Treasuries; Italy truckers strike; Sakharov Prize to ICC

paragraphs.heading: French bonds
paragraphs.body: France's 10-year yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2002, reaching about 5.06%–5.09%, and above the US 10-year Treasury yield for the first time since 2013, Axios and Trading Economics reported. The spread over German Bunds widened to the most since 2011, Disruption Banking reported. AFP tied the sell-off to a budget standoff and violent protests; ECB President Christine Lagarde has been cool on intervening, France 24 reported. [[TAG:danger:yield above 5%]]

paragraphs.heading: Unrest spreads
paragraphs.body: Truck drivers protesting fuel prices disrupted supermarket deliveries across southern Italy, and Spanish unions have called a general strike for November 11, The Rio Times reported. France rejected Trump's attempt to blame its unrest on migration, Al Jazeera reported.

paragraphs.heading: Parliament
paragraphs.body: The European Parliament awarded the Sakharov Prize to the International Criminal Court and backed a non-binding call to add the Houthis to the EU terrorist list, The Rio Times reported.

sections.title: Elections Abroad
sections.summary: Israel's final polls show deadlock before Tuesday; Brazil's Sunday runoff is a dead heat

paragraphs.heading: Israel
paragraphs.body: Final polls before Tuesday's vote show neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's reaching 61 seats; one average has Netanyahu's bloc at 54 and the opposition at 50, Jewish Insider reported, while a Jewish Chronicle analysis said Eisenkot's bloc has widened its lead. Polling is barred from Friday. Israel's High Court barred party poll-watchers from reporting turnout digitally in real time, and Haaretz reported party activists attacked on the trail. [[TAG:warning:deadlock]]

paragraphs.heading: Brazil
paragraphs.body: Sunday's runoff between Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula is a statistical tie: Quaest had Bolsonaro 45% to 44%, Reuters reported via US News, and Datafolha had them at 50% each of valid votes, The Rio Times reported. The Rio Times' average puts Bolsonaro at about 51%. [[TAG:info:Oct 25 runoff]]

sections.title: Global Roundup
sections.summary: WHO warns of 'more complex' Ebola spread; AU condemns Abyei drone strike; Geneva Sudan talks

paragraphs.heading: Ebola
paragraphs.body: The WHO's Africa director warned the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak is growing 'more complex' now that cases are in Congo, Kenya and Nigeria, Al Jazeera reported. Kenya has nine cases in one cluster; Congo has reported about 9,552 cases and 4,602 deaths, though counts vary by source. Officials are investigating whether Nigeria's patient crossed paths with Kenya's first patient at a Ugandan airport. [[TAG:danger:3 countries]]

paragraphs.heading: Sudan
paragraphs.body: The African Union condemned drone strikes in Sudan and Abyei after a strike that Al Jazeera said killed at least 153 people, Radio Dabanga reported. Ceasefire talks resumed in Geneva on October 21 with nearly two dozen countries, UN News reported. The Sudanese pound has fallen to 10,300 per dollar, Dabanga said.
